I couldn't investigate: the Bash tool is denied in this session. Both kubectl calls were rejected with "Permission to use Bash has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode." I have no other tool that can reach the cluster or the metrics endpoint, so I haven't found a root cause and I'm not going to guess at one.

What I was trying to run, all read-only:
- `kubectl -n ledger get pods -o wide` and `get deploy -o wide` to see which ledger-api pods are NotReady and what image or revision they run.
- `kubectl -n ledger rollout history deploy --all` to confirm the 1.4.2 rollout.
- `kubectl -n ledger get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp` to find probe failures, OOM kills, crash loops, or scheduling problems around the time of the rollout.

Next steps that would move this forward:
1. Re-enable Bash for read-only kubectl in namespace `ledger`, or tell me whether a different approach is preferred.
2. If that's not possible, run these yourself and paste the output here:
   - `kubectl -n ledger get pods -o wide`
   - `kubectl -n ledger describe pods -l <ledger-api selector> | grep -A10 -E 'Conditions|Events|Readiness|Last State'`
   - `kubectl -n ledger get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -60`
   - `kubectl -n ledger logs <a-NotReady-pod> --previous` (if it has restarted)
   - Optionally, `promq` for error rate or latency on ledger-api since the 1.4.2 rollout.

With those outputs I can work out the root cause and compare the failing pods against the healthy half.

steps.input: kubectl -n ledger get pods -o wide; kubectl -n ledger get deploy -o wide; kubectl -n ledger rollout history deploy --all 2>&1 | head -50
